transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve gotten so strict about cutting back how much I eat that I hardly feel like I’m taking in anything at all anymore. It's just become a really hard routine to break, and I know I'm barely eating.
Have you experienced significant weight loss since you started restricting your food intake?

My clothes are hanging off me now and people at work and church keep saying I look tiny. But instead of worrying, it actually makes me feel like I’m finally doing something right. I honestly think everyone is overreacting about my weight being too low.
Do you think your weight is at a healthy level right now, or do you still feel like you need to lose more weight?

I feel like I'm doing just fine since I can still work and go hiking, so I think everyone is overreacting about my weight. But when I look in the mirror, I still see my stomach and thighs looking too big, which makes me feel like I need to keep going and stay as small as possible.
When you look in the mirror and see your stomach and thighs as too big, does that thought trigger an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming 'fat'?

Yes, it definitely does. Looking at my stomach and thighs makes me feel like I have to stay as small as possible to be worth anything. It triggers this panicky fear of gaining weight, because I worry that if I blow up, everyone at the warehouse will see me as lazy and unprofessional.
Do you ever experience any episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period, feeling like you can't stop, followed by feelings of guilt or shame?

No, I don't ever have episodes like that at all. My struggle is actually the exact opposite, where I am strictly focused on restricting my food and trying to eat as little as possible. I never lose control or eat large amounts of food.
Do you also engage in excessive exercise or physical activity as a way to further control your weight, in addition to restricting your food intake?
No, I don't engage in excessive exercise to control my weight. I used to go hiking with my club, but lately I haven't had the energy for it at all and have actually had to skip those trips.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by your stomach and thighs looking 'too big' when you look in the mirror, and how that compares to what others see when they look at you?

When I look in the mirror at home or in the locker room, all I can see is my stomach and thighs looking way too big, which makes me feel like I'm not professional or worthy of a promotion. Meanwhile, everyone else tells me my clothes are hanging off me and that I look tiny. Even though they see someone small, I still feel this constant need to keep shrinking just to feel like I'm finally doing something right.
When you see yourself as 'too big' in the mirror, do you think this perception of your body is realistic, or do you recognize that it might be different from how others see you?

To me, what I see in the mirror is completely realistic, and I genuinely feel like my stomach and thighs still need to be smaller. I know my coworkers and the doctor tell me I look tiny, but I think they are overreacting because I can still see areas that need to be trimmed down. I feel completely justified in wanting to keep going because being small is the only way I feel disciplined and worthy.
Do you think you would ever be satisfied with your weight, or is it possible that even if you reached what others consider a very low weight, you would still feel the need to lose more?

Honestly, I don't think I would ever be satisfied and would probably feel the need to keep going. Whenever I lose weight or people tell me I look tiny, it just makes me feel like I'm finally doing something right. It pushes me to want to stay as small as possible just to feel like I have any worth.
